items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: We were living on Henry Clay Avenue then. 711 Henry Clay Avenue.

ctx.x: I can't remember anything definite except that I seemed to have in the back of my mind somewhere this sound of colored women over washing on wash days. You know, the singing with their rough voices, their beautiful roughness, you know, I don't mean a disagreeable word when I say rough. There's a certain beauty in it to me in that voice. One of the nicest things that I know, really, in that particular kind of voice. And I seem to remember an awful lot of that when I was young. And then later on, when I was, must…
Where is Henry Clay? What streets are next to it about?

Henry Clay is two blocks from Audubon Park. Henry Clay and then Calhoun and then Audubon Park. Oh yeah. Oh yeah, sure. It's up in the uptown section. Yeah. And this house was near the, what was then called the Louisiana Retreat. It was a place for insane people. Oh. Uh, what is it called now? Up up at the Magazine Street about? Yeah, it's in between Magazine and uh... St. Charles? Uh, Paria. In between Magazine and Paria. I don't know whether it runs... No, it doesn't run quite to Magazine. It's a couple blocks,…
